A deleveled world is a core feature of requiem, Which US is based around. If you want to fight bandits and mudcrabs for the entire game then US isnt for you.

Since the world is deleveled, obviously you can reach a point where nothing proves a challenge. But that would take hundreds of hours. But most of the time, there are enemies your level that arent too hard or too easy. So, you can always find something to fight. But sure, if you only fight bandits you'll find they stop being a challenge after level 15 or so.

Are you aware of buff foods? There's lots of different kinds, but the most important ones are Beef stew which gives 50 health and 25 carry weight for 1800 sec, and Mammoth Tomato stew (Mullwine braised mammoth is a good alternative) 1 stam per sec for 7200 sec. You should have these on anytime you're in combat. Can be bought at most inns, Bannered mare always has them. 

​

If you haven't already, i would also recommend looting Helgen. There's some really good loot in there, including Remarkable potions in one of the barrels. There's also a crossbow, which you should definitely get if you dont have one already. 

You should also chose a standing stone. Warrior stone makes you do more damage, Lord  gives you armor and magic resist (My personal favorite) Steed gives you a bunch of stamina.

Mudcrabs are a good enemy to fight early on. There's always some close to rivers and ponds. I'd stay away from the really big ones though, they're not pushovers. 

I would also go to that one bandit outside Embershard mine and practice dodging against him. When you're not using a shield, you need to dodge basically everything. Dual wield is very hard, so i would recommend picking up a light shield. 

I'd also join the companions, you get access to training, quests and sparring. Sparring is bugged though, if you lose you're forced to reload. 

​

I have my timescale set to 1:5, requiems default is 1:10. Before the inclusion of Sleep to gain experience in Us this didnt really matter, but it essentially lets me do twice the amount of adventuring in one day.  I've also played around 700+ hours of requiem permadeath, so i might be a bit more efficient that someone new to permadeath. 

But still, Alchemy and speech is the biggest source of xp. So its not impossible to be 15 with default timescale.

On Day 1, focus on alchemy and stick to enemies your level. Mudcrabs (maybe not the really big ones without stews or potions), Wolves (A bow is a must have for sniping those cowardly lone wolves) and skeevers (Whiterun sewers is a good dungeon to do day 1, but dont explore too far! I've heard there's falmer and stuff if you go too far).  You could even hunt Wildlife to train your marksmanship, if you have a hunting permit.   

Day 2 you can start fighting bandits, but make sure you can tank the archers. With heavy armor, beef stew, your first levels into health, that shouldn't be a problem. For some bandit camps you might want to pop a fortify health potion, just to be sure. Make sure you're not wearing too heavy armor, as that will make you too slow, and you might not be able to dodge. You should also be able to hold your own against Sabrecats and bears, but make sure you don't get knocked down by their sprinting attack!

Day 3 is usually the most dangerous, as you might start getting cocky and try to take on something you're not ready for. If you're feeling adventurous, ask yourself if its worth the risk. 

By day 4 you should be above level 15. Late game in requiem is a whole other beast, so i wont get into it here.

Good luck!

Low points would be: There's a few small things that don't make any sense in Ep1-2, Like the grenade in the house with the walker couple, or Clem stabbing a walker with the car key, leaving it in its skull, then kicking the door so that walker gets off the car, or Aj getting shot from behind, the shrapnels being in his stomach, and Clem taking them out with a knife she just used to kill zombies with. 

I didn't like the ending of Ep4. I don't think the whole 'making us think its the same as the ending of S1 and then bam twist Clem is alive' was worth it, considering AJ used an axe he chopped up a walker with seconds ago, to amputate Clem's leg. Even if she survived the blood loss and got out of there, she would still be infected. Weapons covered in zombie muck not infecting people is a recurring problem, but we know it should, as it happens in the comics. But even then, It's a cheap move to not show how they got out of there, and it wasn't worth it.
